_readme.workflow: Edit values under "current" per structure_set, or flip a structure entry's "enabled" to false, then rejoin the world: kubejs/server_scripts/worldgen/structure_overrides.js applies this file at every world load (new chunks only; structure_tag_report.md shows what it did). For category-wide changes ("all villages x0.5") use multipliers in structure_tags.json instead; they apply on top of "current". Re-running tools/gen_structure_config.py is always safe -- it keeps "enabled" and every field you changed in "current".

top_level_fields.source: Where this structure_set's definition came from: a mod jar filename, or "vanilla_known_defaults" (see caveat below).
top_level_fields.structures: The structure(s) this set can place. Each has "structure" (its id), "weight", "enabled" (your on/off switch), and "biomes" (read-only reference).
top_level_fields.original: The values this structure_set actually has without any override -- the diff baseline, refreshed on every scan. Don't edit this; structure_overrides.js compares "current" against it to decide what to write.
top_level_fields.current: Your edits go here. Identical to "original" until you change something.

placement_dials (inside original/current.type: Which placement algorithm: "minecraft:random_spread" (almost everything -- an evenly-spaced grid, one random attempt per cell) or "minecraft:concentric_rings" (strongholds only -- rings expanding out from world spawn, not a grid).
placement_dials (inside original/current.spacing: [random_spread] Average chunks between grid cells, i.e. between attempts at this structure. Bigger spacing = rarer structure. This is usually the dial you want for "make X less/more common".
placement_dials (inside original/current.separation: [random_spread] Minimum chunks kept clear around each grid cell so two attempts can never land right next to each other. Must stay smaller than "spacing" (vanilla convention: separation < spacing, often spacing/4).
placement_dials (inside original/current.spread_type: [random_spread, optional] Where within its grid cell an attempt can land: "linear" (default, anywhere in the cell) or "triangular" (biased toward the cell center -- vanilla only uses this for ocean monuments). Rarely worth touching.
placement_dials (inside original/current.spread: [concentric_rings] Random jitter added within a ring so structures aren't on a perfect circle.
placement_dials (inside original/current.count: [concentric_rings] Total number of attempts across every ring in the whole set (128 for vanilla strongholds). Lower = fewer strongholds total, still spread across the same ring layout.
placement_dials (inside original/current.frequency: A flat 0.0-1.0 chance multiplier applied on top of spacing/separation or the ring layout -- "of the grid cells that pass everything else, only spawn here X% of the time." Vanilla uses this to keep mineshafts/buried treasure rare despite a 1-chunk grid. Setting it to 0 disables the structure outright -- this is exactly what structure_overrides.js does automatically when you disable every structure in a set. Omitted/1.0 means "no extra reduction".
placement_dials (inside original/current.frequency_reduction_method: Which RNG algorithm applies the "frequency" chance ("legacy_type_1" / "legacy_type_2" / "default"). Purely about matching vanilla's exact RNG behavior bit-for-bit -- doesn't change how rare something ends up feeling. Safe to leave alone.
placement_dials (inside original/current.salt: Seeds this structure_set's own slice of the world seed's RNG, so different structure_sets don't land in lockstep with each other. Only affects WHERE on the grid attempts fall, not how often. Safe to leave alone -- a wrong value just shifts the grid's phase relative to a from-scratch vanilla world.
placement_dials (inside original/current.locate_offset: The "xyz coords" dial: an integer [x, y, z] nudge applied to every placement attempt before any other check. x/z shift the whole grid sideways; y is essentially unused (the structure's own logic picks its actual height). Default [0, 0, 0].

per_structure_fields (inside a structure.weight: When a set holds multiple structures sharing one grid (e.g. the 5 village variants in minecraft:villages), weight influences which ONE wins a given grid cell before that structure's own biome check narrows it further. Only meaningful relative to the other entries in the same set.
per_structure_fields (inside a structure.enabled: Your removal switch. false on the only structure in a set forces that set's frequency to 0 (always schema-safe). false on one of several removes just that entry from the set's structure list, leaving the others untouched.
per_structure_fields (inside a structure.biomes: Read-only reference -- which biomes this structure can spawn in, from the mod's own structure json or (vanilla) minecraft's has_structure/* tags. Changing WHERE something spawns needs editing the structure's own definition, which this framework deliberately never touches -- see the README.
per_structure_fields (inside a structure.blocked: Read-only, only present when another mod stops this structure in code (YUNG's "Disable Vanilla X" options, Better Dungeons' small nether dungeon toggle). Its set can still be tuned, but nothing generates while the block is on. Written by the scanner from the current mod configs; re-run it after changing one of those options.

_readme.caveats: Vanilla "source":"vanilla_known_defaults" entries come from a table in the scanner (vanilla bootstraps them in Java, unlike every mod here), javap-checked against the 1.19.2 StructureSets bytecode. /dumpstructuregen in-world shows the live values. Also: this pack's minecraft:villages and minecraft:end_cities are NOT vanilla -- Terralith and Nullscape already override them, and the scanner picked that up (check "source" per entry).

structures.blocked: YUNG's Better Dungeons stops it in code (config/betterdungeons-forge-1_19.toml: "Enable Small Nether Dungeons" = false). Tuning this set has no effect.
YUNG's Better Desert Temples stops it in code (config/betterdeserttemples-forge-1_19.toml: "Disable Vanilla Pyramids" = true). Tuning this set has no effect.
YUNG's Better Jungle Temples stops it in code (config/betterjungletemples-forge-1_19_2.toml: "Disable Vanilla Jungle Temples" = true). Tuning this set has no effect.
YUNG's Better Nether Fortresses stops it in code (config/betterfortresses-forge-1_19.toml: "Disable Vanilla Nether Fortresses" = true). Tuning this set has no effect.
YUNG's Better Strongholds always stops it (no config option). Tuning this set has no effect.
YUNG's Better Witch Huts stops it in code (config/betterwitchhuts-forge-1_19.toml: "Disable Vanilla Witch Huts" = true). Tuning this set has no effect.
